title: Implement a Scheduled Data Retention Policy Manager
description: The SwiftSlate data warehouse is continuously ingesting data, leading to significant storage growth. To manage costs and comply with data governance standards, a new automated data retention feature is required. This task involves implementing a new scheduled job within the `scheduler_service` that periodically purges data from the storage layer older than a configurable threshold. This task is broken into several distinct stages to simulate a realistic, multi-session development workflow, testing the agent's ability to retain context and build upon previous work.

project_spec.name: SwiftSlate Productivity Warehouse
project_spec.description:
SwiftSlate Productivity Warehouse is an expert-grade, C-based data-warehouse solution whose primary mission is to **maximize analyst and engineer throughput**.  By treating every data-handling concern—ingestion, validation, transformation, storage, quality-assurance, analytics, visualization, and monitoring—as first-class layers, SwiftSlate shortens feedback loops and radically reduces the time required to turn raw operational data into actionable insight.

The system is organized as an end-to-end productivity pipeline: high-velocity event streams enter the *Ingress Layer* (Kafka-like stream façade + bulk batch gateway), traverse the *Validation & Transformation Layer* (plug-in Strategy Pattern for rule sets), settle inside the *Data Lake & Warehouse Layer* (columnar store, hot/cold tiers), and finally surface through the *Productivity Services Layer* (self-service scheduling, visual dashboards, alerting).  Under the hood, an ETL_Pipeline orchestrated by a domain-specific scheduler exploits fine-grained parallel_processing, while the Observer_Pattern notifies downstream micro-services of data_quality_checks and error_recovery events, enabling continuous monitoring and auto-healing.  Together these layers deliver near-real-time insights and dramatically cut the “data-to-decision” latency for knowledge workers.

With 89 curated C source/header files (≈718 k tokens), the codebase cleanly separates concerns: batch_processing and stream_processing are isolated into micro-services that communicate over event buses; data_storage adapters abstract multiple back ends; a unified monitoring façade aggregates metrics; and extensible Strategy objects empower teams to add new transformations without touching core logic.  The result is a highly productive environment where developers, data engineers, and business users can iterate rapidly without cross-team bottlenecks.
dependencies: libpq (PostgreSQL C client) – warehouse & metadata catalog
jansson – JSON parsing for data_ingestion & configuration
cURL/libcurl – REST hooks for monitoring & visualization layer
